comparison: Both evaluate the core flip-flop-fix mechanism (C20-C22, C36-C37, C59-C60). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with emphasis on validation through efficiency matching and reproducibility across simulations. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, calling it 'solid' and 'a strong point of the study', affirming the ligand flip observations across multiple simulations and ligands.

Both address efficiency calculations (C23, C54, C90). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the excellent match despite absolute energy discrepancies. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'simulated efficiencies were a good representation of experimental measures' and noting this as a strength.

Both evaluate binding energy calculations (C51-C53, C87-C88). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging limitations but emphasizing that efficiency ratios are accurately captured. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing significant concerns about 'up to 130% errors' and accuracy issues that 'raise some doubt as to the validity of the simulations'. This represents a key disagreement.

Both evaluate docking results (C25-C28, C44-C45). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting consistency across agonists and poses. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, stating 'Docking results are clearly presented and remarkably consistent' and finding 'the premise for the simulations to be good'. Strong agreement on this aspect.

Both address MD simulation quality and convergence (C29-C33). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing RMSD convergence and RMSF patterns as evidence of technical quality. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about 'brevity of the simulations', 'lack of scope', and 'limited timescales (200 ns)'. Disagreement on adequacy of simulation methodology.

Both evaluate PCA-derived intermediate states (C46-C50). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting consistency across agonists and BPMD validation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether 'landscapes constructed on two principal components...are highly robust or reproducible'. Mixed acceptance of intermediate state concept but doubt about characterization robustness.

Both address the 'fix' structural changes (C55-C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting quantification and consistency across agonists. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting 'structural rationale...on the basis of pocket volume, hydration, and rearrangement of key residues'. Agreement on these structural observations.

Both evaluate alignment with experimental structures (C38-C39, C41-C43). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing cryo-EM alignment and extended stability. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, noting 'convergence of agonist-docked simulations towards a desensitized state' and viewing alignment with cryo-EM as validation.

Both address loop C mechanism and integration with mutagenesis (C63-C64, C68-C70, C111-C112). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, integrating simulation with experimental data. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, consistent with acceptance of the overall flip-flop-fix mechanism and structure-function integration.

Both evaluate detailed structural characterization of states and transitions (C71-C79). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, providing mechanistic insights from Figure 6 and videos. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED as part of the accepted flip-flop mechanism, with no specific challenges to these interaction details.

Both address salt bridge dynamics and agonist-specific effects (C80-C86). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, correlating with mutagenesis data. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, viewing this as successful integration of computational and experimental approaches consistent with overall positive assessment.

Both evaluate justification for ECD dimer model (C34-C35, C91-C93). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing excellent match between dimer simulations and pentamer experiments. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the simplified model validation, though binding energy accuracy issues temper this support.

Both address reinterpretation of αY190-αD200 interaction (C113-C117). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanism remains unclear and interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, not challenging this reinterpretation and viewing it as consistent with the accepted flip-flop-fix mechanism. Mild disagreement on confidence level.

Both evaluate methodological implications and applications (C90, C126-C128). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing efficiency calculation accuracy as validating the approach. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about 'motivations for and limitations' of the approximate model and questioning generalizability for drug discovery given accuracy issues.

OpenEval evaluates background claims about AChR structure and function (C1-C19) as SUPPORTED, noting they represent established knowledge with proper citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background material.

OpenEval evaluates control simulations (C41-C43) as SUPPORTED, noting pentamer-dimer comparison and apo simulations strengthen confidence. While peer R8 partially overlaps (C41-C43), it focuses on cryo-EM alignment rather than control experiment validation specifically.

OpenEval evaluates the reverse docking control experiment (C44-C45) as SUPPORTED, noting it demonstrates protein structure favors trans binding. While peer R4 includes these claims, it focuses on initial docking consistency rather than this specific control experiment's implications.

OpenEval evaluates quantitative characterization of flip and flop movements (C59-C62) as SUPPORTED. While peer R1 includes C59-C60, OpenEval R12 specifically addresses the lack of correlation between loop C displacement and functional parameters (C62), which is not explicitly discussed by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates the 'slippery anchor' mechanism (C69-C70) as SUPPORTED with quantitative distance measurements. While peer R9 includes these claims, it groups them with broader loop C mechanism rather than specifically evaluating the slippery anchor model.

OpenEval evaluates structural assignment evidence and limitations (C87-C89) as SUPPORTED while acknowledging absence of direct experimental structures. Peer R3 includes C87-C88 but focuses on binding energy accuracy concerns rather than the broader question of structural assignment validation.

OpenEval evaluates broader context and generality of ligand reorientation mechanisms (C94-C98) as SUPPORTED, citing other systems and acknowledging limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates characterization of intermediate m2 state (C99-C100) as SUPPORTED, noting agonist-dependent stability differences. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses the m2 intermediate characterization, though peer R6 discusses intermediate states more generally.

OpenEval evaluates integration of loop C literature with simulation results (C101-C104) as SUPPORTED, reconciling apparent contradictions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this literature integration.

OpenEval evaluates experimental mutagenesis data on loop C function (C105-C108) as SUPPORTED, drawing inferences about agonist-dependent vs independent activation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mutagenesis interpretations.

OpenEval evaluates αY190 mutagenesis integration (C109-C112) as SUPPORTED, explaining functional importance through structural mechanism. While peer R9 includes C111-C112, OpenEval R23 specifically addresses the mutagenesis data integration (C109-C110) not explicitly discussed by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates broader structural biology context (C118-C122) as SUPPORTED, citing enzyme systems and other receptors. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual comparisons to other protein systems.

OpenEval evaluates loop E function and efficiency classes (C123-C125) as SUPPORTED, citing experimental data and making logical inferences. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these claims about efficiency class structure.

OpenEval evaluates the central mechanistic proposal that flip initiates affinity increase (C128) as SUPPORTED but requiring experimental validation. While peer R14 includes C128, it focuses on methodological approach rather than specifically evaluating this mechanistic ordering hypothesis.
